Title: Privy vs Turnkey (2026): Pricing, Architecture, and Fit
# Privy vs Turnkey (2026): Pricing, Architecture, and Fit. Joan Alavedra, Co-Founder at Openfort•6 min read. Side-by-side comparison of Privy and Turnkey wallet infrastructure. The wallet stack you own. Privy and Turnkey both let you give users a wallet without a seed phrase, and that is where the similarity ends. Privy is a bundled product you drop in. Turnkey is a signing primitive you build on. Picking wrongly costs you either six months of building auth you did not want to build, or a migration when the bundle stops fitting. Pick **Privy** if you want wallets, login, and fiat onramps from one SDK, you are happy inside Stripe's ecosystem, and your users transact often enough that per-user pricing works out. Pick **Turnkey** if you are assembling your own stack, you need per-signature economics because most of your wallets sit idle, or you need key-quorum approvals and a policy engine. | **What it is** | Bundled wallets, auth, and onramps | Key management and signing infrastructure |. | **Entry pricing** | Free to 499 MAU, then 299 USD/month | Free to 100 wallets and 25 signatures, then 0.10 USD/signature |. | **Volume pricing** | 499 USD/month to 9,999 MAU, then enterprise | 99 USD/month Pro at 0.05 USD/signature, enterprise from 0.0015 USD |. Model your own numbers before you pick, because the same application can be three times cheaper on either one:. * A consumer app with 50,000 registered wallets where 2,000 people log in monthly and each signs twice: Privy's Scale tier at 499 USD/month covers it. On Turnkey PAYG that is 4,000 signatures at 0.10 USD, so 400 USD, but you have blown through the 1,000-wallet cap and need Pro or enterprise. * A trading or agent workload with 500 wallets signing 200 times each per month: 100,000 signatures. On Turnkey Pro that is 99 USD plus 5,000 USD. For a fintech that wants fiat in and stablecoins out, that is a lot of work you do not have to do. What you get is a signing primitive with a policy engine and key-quorum approvals on top, and what you build is everything a user actually sees.

Openfort uses transparent usage-based pricing where an operation is defined as creating a wallet or sending a transaction. You only pay for what you use, which means applications with many registered users but lower transaction volumes aren't penalized the way MAU-based models are. Openfort bills per operation with unlimited transaction volume and every feature on the free tier (no feature gating), so you never pay for dormant wallets or hit feature gates as you grow. Privy charges based on monthly active users: free under 499 MAUs, then $299/month for up to 2,500 MAUs (Core tier), with usage-based billing kicking in above 10,000 MAUs, 50,000 monthly signatures, or $1M monthly transaction volume.
